A. FACTUAL MATRIX 1.

The present complaint has been filed under section 138 of the Negotiable Instrume Act, 1881 (hereinafter "NI Act") by Sh. Balvinder Singh hereinafter "complainant") again Sh. Surinder Singh hereinafter "accused").
2.

The substance of allegations, as contained in the complaint, are as follows:
1. That the accused is known to the complainant very well and had been maintaining good friendly and visiting terms with the complainant since long, as the accused and the complainant both are living in the same locality.
2. That as the accused was in dire need of money to meet his some urgent financial requirement, hence, the accused inm the month of August, 2016 had approached in the mont of August, 2016 had approached the complainant and requested to provide him a financial assistance to the tune of Rs. 90,000/ and promised to return/ refund the said amount to complainant within a period of six months.
3. That the complainant being wellwisher of the accused and considering his reques genuine had agreed to help the accused and after arranging the funds from his sources, t complainant gave a sum of Rs. 90,000/ to the accused on his assurances to repay the sam within the agreed period.

4. That accordingly, in discharge of his abovesaid legal enforceable debts and liabi repay the abovesaid amount to the complainant, the accused had issued a cheque bearing n 051282 dt. 28.04.2017 for a sum of Rs. 90,000/ drawn on Ramgarhia Cooperative Bank Ltd.
,Vishnu Garden Branch, New Delhi, in favour of the complainant with the assurances that  said cheque would be honoured on its presentation for encashment by the complainant.

5. That as per the above commitment and instructions of the accused, the complainant presented the abovesaid cheque for encashment with his banker i.e. Yes bank, Ltd., Tilak Nagar Branch, New Delhi110018, but to the utter shock and surprise of the complainant, 
abovesaid cheque got dishonoured and returned unpaid to the complainant with the remarks "funds insufficient" vide cheque return memo dt. 02.05.2017.
6.

That immediately after receiving the abovesaid cheque as dishonoured, the complainant contacted and informed the accused about the fate of the said cheque and demanded his money in cash, but the accused did not give any satisfactory reply and avoi the complainant on one pretext or the other and ultimately flatly refused to pay even a  penny to the complainant.

Thus, it is quite clear that the acc issued the abovesaid cheque knowing fully well that the same would not be honoured on it presentation before the bank by the complainant and made false representation and assurances to the complainant.

8. That the complainant had advanced the abovesaid amount to the accused on his assurance to repay the same to the complainant within the agreed period, which the accus has failed to do so, and hence in view of the above conduct of the accused, it becomes c that the accused has caused wrongful loss to the complainant and wrongful gain to himsel and hence, the abovesaid act and conduct of the accused rendered him liable to be dealt  under the provisions of Sections 138 NI Act.
Besides this, the accused is also liable to prosecuted for the criminal offences u/s 406/420 of Indian Penal Code.

9. That finding no other alternative the complainant through his advocate got sent  notice his advocate got sent a legal notice dt. 30.052017 to the accused by way of speed AD as well as courier, whereby the accused was called upon to make payment of the abovesaid dishonoured cheque to the complainant within a period of 15 days of the receip legal notice.

The said notice was sent at the correct address of the accused and the sam been duly served upon the accused through speed post as well as courier, but the accused despite receipt of the said legal notice has neither made the payment of the above chequ amount nor sent any reply to the said legal notice till date, hence the present complain being filed before this Hon'ble Court.
B. PRESUMMONING EVIDENCE & NOTICE 3.

Presummoning evidence was led by the complainant and on finding a prima facie case,
the accused was summoned to face trial vide order dated 22.07.2017.
Notice against the accused was framed on 08.02.2019.
He took the following plea of defence at the stage of framing of notice:
I know the complainant since last 34 years.
As the complainant has a scooter mechanic shop which I used to visit.
I had obtained finance of Rs. 20,000/ on an Activa scooter from the complainant and had given the cheque in question alongwith certain documentary proofs to the complainant.
I have already paid the amount.
Despite my requests, the complainant did not transfer the RC to my name.
The complainant has misuse the cheque in question.
He admitted the signatures on the cheque in question and also admitted the receipt of le demand notice at this stage.

E. INGREDIENTS OF OFFENCE UNDER SECTION 138 OF NI ACT 8.
Before dwelling into the facts of the present case, it would be pertinent to dis legal standards required to be met by both sides.

In order to establish the offence unde Section 138 of NI Act, the prosecution must fulfil all the essential ingredients of the  as highlighted below:
 The cheque was drawn by a person on an account maintained by him/her for payment of money and the same is presented for payment within a period of 3 months from the date which it is drawn or within the period of its validity;
The cheque was drawn by the drawer for discharge of any legally enforceable debt other liability;

The drawer fails to make payment of the said amount of money within fifteen days from the date of receipt of notice.
9. In addition to the above, the conditions stipulated under Section 142 NI Act hav be fulfilled.
10. ANALYSIS OF VARIOUS INGREDIENTS OF THE OFFENCE
The complainant has proved the original cheques, Ex.CW1/1, which the accused has not disputed as being drawn on the account of the accused.
He has also admitted his signatures on the cheque.
The cheque in question was returned unpaid vide Ex. CW1/2.
The same has also been proved by the complainant.
As per Section 146 of NI Act, Bank's slip is prima facie evid of proof of dishonor.
The accused has not disputed the same.
The complainant has proved on record legal notice Ex. CW1/3.
The same has been admitted by the accused at the stage of framing of notice u/s 251 Cr.P.C. and at the sta statement of accused u/s 313 Cr.P.C and in his cross examination.
The fact that the payment was not made within 15 days of the receipt of the lega notice is also not disputed.
As such, on the basis of the above, the first, fourth and f ingredient of the offence under Section 138 NI Act stands proved against the accused.
11. The controversy in the present complaint case pertains to second ingredient.
PRESUMPTIONS UNDER NI ACT 12.
As far as the proof of second ingredient is concerned, the complainant is require prove that the cheque in question was drawn by the drawer for discharging a legally enforceable debt.
As per the scheme of the NI Act, once the accused admits signature on  cheque in question, certain presumptions are drawn, which result in shifting of onus on  accused.

13. The combined effect of section 118(a) NI Act and section 139 of the NI Act is th presumption exists that the cheque was drawn for consideration and given by the accused  the discharge of debt or other liability.

In Hiten P. Dalal v. Bratindranath Banerjee (2 6 SCC 16), their Lordships of Hon'ble Supreme Court observed as follows:
Because both Sections 138 and 139 require that the Court "shall presume" the liability o drawer of the cheques for the amounts for which the cheques are drawn, as noted in State  Digitally  signed by   KARANBIR KARANBIR SINGH SINGH Date:

25.1. Once the execution of cheque is admitted Section 139 of theAct mandates a presumption that the cheque was for the discharge of any debt or other liability.
25.2. The presumption under Section 139 is a rebuttable presumption and the onus is on t accused to raise probable defence.
The standard of proof for rebutting the presumption i that of preponderance of probabilities.
25.3. To rebut the presumption, it is open for the accused to rely on evidence led by hi the accused can also rely on the materials submitted by the complainant in order to rais probable defence.
Inference of preponderance of probabilities can be drawn not only from the materials brought on record by the parties but also by reference to the circumstance upon which they rely.
